about.title: Sierra Madre Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Sierra Madre's small-town charm, from its tree-lined streets to shops along Sierra Madre Boulevard, doesn't make property owners immune to keeping their spaces safe. Whether the fall happened on a cracked sidewalk near Lima Street, in a store along Michillinda Avenue, or inside a private residence, California law asks a specific question: did the property owner know, or should they have known, about the hazard, and did they fail to fix it or warn you? That single issue often decides a claim. LawProactive connects Sierra Madre residents and visitors who've been hurt in a fall with an independent attorney who understands how to investigate these cases, from tracking down surveillance footage before it's erased to documenting the hazard itself. There's no cost to get connected, and no fee unless the attorney recovers compensation for you. You focus on healing; let someone else sort out the legal footwork.

whyChoose.title: Why Sierra Madre Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California premises liability claims hinge on proving the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help gather evidence, like maintenance logs or prior complaints, that shows this.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to preserve that video can make the difference in a claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Sink Your Case
items.desc: Even if you were partly distracted or not watching your step, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows recovery, just reduced by your share of responsibility.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Sierra Madre?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, such as a city building or public sidewalk, that window can be much shorter, so it's worth getting advice sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if the fall happened at a small shop on Sierra Madre Boulevard and no one saw it?
items.answer: Lack of witnesses doesn't end your options. An attorney can look for surveillance cameras nearby, request incident reports, and interview employees or other customers who may have noticed the hazard beforehand.

items.question: Will it hurt my claim if I was partly at fault for not seeing the hazard?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California follows a pure comparative fault system, meaning you can still recover damages even if you share some blame, though your compensation would be reduced proportionally.
